comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the SNX4 knockout validation (C26-C29). OpenEval emphasizes the progressive depletion and validation methods, while Reviewer 1 praises the 'sequential characterization' and 'novel in vitro model.' Strong agreement on knockout efficiency.

OpenEval finds neuronal morphology data (C30-C32) well-controlled and supporting specificity. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Reviewer 1 noting concerns about statistical presentation of Sholl analysis (missing cell numbers, standard deviations). Agreement on findings but disagreement on rigor of presentation.

Both strongly support the electrophysiological findings (C3, C4, C33-C34, C37-C39, C41, C45, C103). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation, while peer reviewers (R1, R2, editor) describe data as 'convincing' and 'solid.' Strong concordance on frequency-dependent enhancement and vesicle recruitment.

Both support baseline synaptic property measurements (C36, C40, C42-C43). OpenEval emphasizes these establish specificity of the effect, while Reviewer 2 accepts that 'measures of release probability were unaffected.' Agreement that SNX4 affects sustained activity rather than basal release.

Both support the overexpression control (C44). OpenEval notes it controls for artifacts, peer reviewers accept it without question as supporting rescue specificity. Full agreement on this control experiment.

Both support the recycling/endocytosis findings (C5, C47-C54). OpenEval emphasizes complementary methods and temperature controls, while Reviewer 2 accepts the negative result noting it 'may be intuitively closer to the endosome function.' Agreement that SNX4 doesn't affect recycling, though this contrasts with expected endosomal roles.

OpenEval supports VAMP2 measurements (C7, C55-C60) as consistent across assays. Peer reviewers express uncertainty: Reviewer 1 questions the Sholl analysis pattern, Reviewer 3 suggests static measurements are insufficient and wants 'real-time VAMP2 trafficking.' Disagreement on adequacy of the approach.

Both support autophagy flux measurements (C6, C61-C66). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls (bafilomycin) and multiple markers. Reviewer 1 states experiments are 'well conducted' but notes they 'do not assist for the explanation of the molecular mechanism.' Agreement on data quality, but peer review notes limited mechanistic insight.

Both support increased docked vesicles finding (C8, C70-C71). OpenEval provides detailed validation of quantitative measurements, while Reviewers 1 and 2 describe EM data as 'convincing' and accept this as a 'key structural finding.' Strong agreement on this central phenotype.

Both support normal vesicle numbers and size (C9, C67-C69). OpenEval emphasizes this establishes specificity, while Reviewer 2 highlights this as 'a novel finding' distinguishing SNX4 from other endosomal proteins. Strong agreement on the significance of this negative result.

OpenEval supports active zone length and structural measurements (C10, C72-C75) as well-defined and quantified. Peer reviewers express uncertainty: Reviewer 1 asks how increased active synapses, shorter AZ, and higher docked vesicles relate to each other. Data accepted but interpretation questioned.

Both support the integrated finding of increased docked vesicle density (C11, C76). OpenEval notes appropriate integration of docking and AZ length changes, Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'alteration in synapse ultrastructure' as demonstrated. Agreement on this key ultrastructural phenotype.

OpenEval supports the summary conclusions (C12, C13, C98) as well-supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty: all reviewers note lack of mechanistic understanding, with Reviewer 2 stating 'It is unclear how the endosomal sorting proteins...are connected to presynaptic...function.' Agreement on phenomenology but disagreement on mechanistic support.

OpenEval supports the logical reasoning about release probability (C100-C102, C107), noting it addresses alternative explanations with data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this reasoning chain.

Both support the distinction from other endosomal proteins (C83-C84). OpenEval identifies this as novel based on EM data, Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges 'a novel finding in endosomal protein knock-out studies.' Strong agreement on scientific significance of this distinction.

OpenEval supports contextualization claims (C77-C82) including speculative model (C79-C80). Peer reviewers note uncertainty: Reviewer 1 states presentation is 'mostly descriptive' and would benefit from mechanistic speculation, Reviewer 3 cites 'lack of mechanism' as weakness. Both note speculation but peer review emphasizes insufficiency.

Both rate speculative mechanisms (C93-C95, plus C78-C80 overlap) as uncertain. OpenEval explicitly notes these are 'hypotheses for future work rather than demonstrated findings.' Peer reviewers similarly note lack of mechanistic support. Strong agreement that speculation is reasonable but unproven.
OpenEval supports background/context claims (C1-C2, C14-C25) as appropriately cited but not novel findings. No specific peer review evaluation addresses these background claims separately.

OpenEval rates novelty and mechanistic claims (C85-C90, C96-C97, C99, C108) as uncertain, noting C97 requires literature verification. Peer reviewers support the novelty claim (C97): editor calls study 'important,' Reviewer 1 notes it 'tackles an open and yet unresolved question.' Disagreement on novelty assessment.
